locator: Article body, paragraphs 3-4 (Canal Road plant tour)
shows: A MercerMe article of July 31, 2025 reports a tour of New Jersey American Water's Canal Road plant. It says that the Canal Road and Raritan-Millstone plants together currently deliver about 180 million gallons of treated water a day under peak demand, with another 90 million gallons a day of reserve capacity. It quotes NJAW's Senior Production Manager: the Canal Road plant alone has a firm capacity of 80 million gallons a day, and 'We are currently peaking at about 180 million combined systemwide.'
limits: A news report of a spoken, rounded figure ('about 180 million'), not a metered record. It does not give the date of the peak day or say that it is the highest day on record; it is the summer 2025 peak. It is production of the whole system, so it includes the water sold to other systems and the transfers to other NJAWC systems. The reserve figure is not a rated capacity.

The plant maxima may fall on different days, so their sum is not a highest day of the system. The figures are for 2023 and 2021-2023, not the scenario year.

locator: Water Supply Firm Capacity line; Water Demand table; Water Supply Deficit or Surplus table; Glossary of Terms (Current Peak Demand, Firm Capacity)
shows: The NJDEP record for the New Jersey American Water Raritan System (PWSID 2004002), last updated January 30, 2024, gives a water supply firm capacity of 245.155 MGD. NJDEP defines firm capacity as the pumping or treatment capacity that meets peak daily demand with the largest pumping or treatment unit out of service. The record gives a current peak daily demand of 160.922 MGD for July 2020, plus a committed peak of 4.460 MGD, for a total peak of 165.382 MGD and a firm capacity surplus of 79.773 MGD. The glossary says that the current peak demand is the average day of the highest demand month in the last five years, on 31 days: 4,988.577 million gallons in July 2020. The highest yearly demand is 50,802.390 million gallons in 2021.
limits: Firm capacity is less than the total rated capacity, because it leaves out the largest unit; it is a floor on what the plants and wells can produce with their controls working. The record does not list the plants and wells that it sums. The 160.922 MGD is the average day of the peak month, not a highest day, and it can include water that the system sells to other systems and contract commitments. The record is self-reported to the regulator and is dated January 2024.
